sheet-1.description: The left half of sheet 1 of the 1930 Sanborn atlas of Paramus, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows a straight stretch of Fairview Avenue (today North Farview Avenue) in central Paramus, about 2,500 feet long, with house numbers 1501 to 1559, crossed two thirds of the way down by Sprout Brook Road, whose line survives as Century Road and East Century Road. The district is thinly built: scattered one and two storey frame dwellings, auto garages and a few outbuildings stand along both sides of Fairview Avenue, with deep undivided lots behind them in blocks 36, 37, 43 and 44. The largest building is the Fairview School on the west side of the avenue north of Sprout Brook Road, a brick and frame building heated by steam with electric light. Near the junction stand a few concrete-block dwellings, and south of Sprout Brook Road a small group of houses and a gasoline tank. Apart from Sprout Brook Road no cross street is drawn; the lines running off Fairview Avenue are lot lines. The top and bottom margins are marked no exposures. The right half of the sheet, outside this part, carries the key map of the whole borough, the index of streets and specials, and notes on water facilities and the volunteer fire department, which are not part of the to-scale map.
notes: Fairview Avenue is today North Farview Avenue.
Sprout Brook Road is today Century Road (west of Farview) and East Century Road (east of Farview); identified from its position and bearing.

Placed from the single junction of Fairview Avenue and Sprout Brook Road, with the rotation of its drawn lines and an assumed scale of 4.13 px per ft (the fitted scale of both parts of sheet 3, which draw the same avenue; the scale bar gives 3.92): low confidence.

Scale 100 ft. Left half: Fairview Avenue (house numbers 1501-1559) with Sprout Brook Road crossing it, Fairview School; one part (config sheet-1). Right half is the key map of the town (about 1800 ft to an inch), the index of streets and specials and the water-facilities and fire-department notes; not a to-scale part and left out of the mask. Sprout Brook Road is today's Century Road / East Century Road. Only one junction: anchored part.

sheet-2-1.description: The lower part of sheet 2 of the 1930 Sanborn atlas of Paramus, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 35 degrees so that Midland Avenue runs across the page. It covers Midland Avenue (house numbers 225 to 303) east of Paramus Road, with Cedar Lane running south from it to Midwood Road at the bottom of the sheet. This was the civic centre of the borough in 1930: on the south side of Midland Avenue stand the Paramus Fire Company No. 3 engine house (concrete block) and, on Cedar Lane, the Paramus Community Church, heated by steam with electric light, drawn from plans. Around them are one and two storey frame dwellings, auto garages, several greenhouses, on large lots in blocks 23, 28 and 29. Midwood Road, with house numbers 701 to 732, has a short row of dwellings at its junction with Cedar Lane. Much of the part is open farmland with only lot lines drawn; the north and south margins are marked no exposures. Midland Avenue is drawn 33 feet wide and Cedar Lane 30 feet. The part above the heavy line on the same sheet shows the western end of Midland Avenue at Paramus Road.
notes: Placed from two junctions on Cedar Lane (Midland Avenue and Midwood Road) as a helmert: low confidence; the fitted scale (4.18 px per ft) is about 6 percent larger than the scale bar.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts drawn at the same rotation, separated by a heavy line: part 1 (bottom) Midland Avenue east of the Saddle River with Cedar Lane and Midwood Road, Paramus Fire Co. No. 3, Paramus Community Church; part 2 (top) Paramus Road with Central Avenue, Coolidge Place and Midland Avenue, Midland School, Saddle River.

sheet-2-2.description: The upper part of sheet 2 of the 1930 Sanborn atlas of Paramus, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 35 degrees. It shows the junction of Paramus Road and Midland Avenue in the northwest of the borough, next to the Saddle River and the Ridgewood borough line. Paramus Road (house numbers 701 to 730) crosses the left of the part; Central Avenue leaves it to the east and turns into Coolidge Place, which runs back south to Midland Avenue. Midland Avenue (house numbers 201 to 276) runs east along the bottom of the part, and its continuation west of Paramus Road, labelled only Road, crosses the Saddle River. The largest building is Midland School, a brick school heated by steam, in block 23; west of it stands the Borough Hall, a small frame building near Midland Avenue. Along Paramus Road are an auto repair garage with gasoline tanks, a mushroom farm restaurant and a scattering of dwellings; the blocks along Central Avenue and Coolidge Place hold frame houses with auto garages, in blocks 22, 24 and 27. The rest is open land with lot lines, marked no exposures at the top. Streets are drawn 40 feet wide, Midland Avenue 33 feet. The Saddle River and the borough limit run along the left edge.
notes: The bend where Central Avenue turns into Coolidge Place is drawn about 15 m from today's corner, so it was not used.
Placed from three junctions (Paramus Road with Central Avenue and Midland Avenue, Coolidge Place with Midland Avenue) with a first-order fit and no redundancy: medium to low confidence.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts drawn at the same rotation, separated by a heavy line: part 1 (bottom) Midland Avenue east of the Saddle River with Cedar Lane and Midwood Road, Paramus Fire Co. No. 3, Paramus Community Church; part 2 (top) Paramus Road with Central Avenue, Coolidge Place and Midland Avenue, Midland School, Saddle River.

sheet-3-1.description: The right part of sheet 3 of the 1930 Sanborn atlas of Paramus, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 36 degrees so that Fairview Avenue runs diagonally down the page. It covers Fairview Avenue (today South Farview Avenue, house numbers 1301 to 1380) from Fairmount Place south to Pleasant Avenue, at the southern edge of the borough near Rochelle Park and Maywood. On the east side Aradale Road has a row of small new houses on narrow lots, and Mildred Avenue (drawn 25 feet wide) and Gertrude Avenue lead to further house lots in blocks 53, 54, 57 and 58. West of Fairview Avenue a newer subdivision of Cloverdale and Westview Avenues ends at Ridgeland Road, its blocks 55, 56 and 61 densely filled with one and two storey dwellings, some of concrete block, and a few stores. The Fairview Fire Company No. 1 stands on the east side of Fairview Avenue north of Aradale Road, and a single larger stone or concrete building stands alone in block 52. Pleasant Avenue runs along the bottom, with a trolley right of way beside it. The top of the part shows Fairmount Place, which is also drawn at the foot of the left part of the sheet.
notes: Aradale Road is today Ardale Road.
Fairview Avenue is today South Farview Avenue.
Pleasant Avenue appears displaced against its modern line (junctions 14 to 15 m off), so it was not used.
The fitted scale (4.16 px per ft) is about 6 percent larger than the scale bar.
Gertrude Avenue at Mildred Avenue is a hand-picked point.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy dog-legged line: part 1 (right, turned about 36 degrees) Fairview Avenue from Fairmount Place south to Pleasant Avenue with Aradale Road, Mildred, Gertrude, Cloverdale, Westview Avenues and Ridgeland Road, Fairview Fire Co. No. 1; part 2 (left, north nearly up) Fairview Avenue from Prospect Street to Fairmount Place with Fairview Terrace, Maple, Spring Valley, Richard and Helen Avenues. Fairmount Place is drawn on both parts.

sheet-3-2.description: The left part of sheet 3 of the 1930 Sanborn atlas of Paramus, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north nearly up. It shows Fairview Avenue (today North and South Farview Avenue, house numbers 1401 to 1483) running straight down the page from Prospect Street to Fairmount Place in the south of the borough. Side streets leave it on both sides: Prospect and Fairview Terrace to the west at the top, Maple Avenue to the west and Spring Valley Avenue to the east in the middle, and Richard Avenue (marked not open), Helen Avenue and Fairmount Place to the east further south. The blocks (43 to 52) hold one and two storey frame dwellings with auto garages, a filling station with gasoline tanks on the east side of Fairview Avenue, a small printing shop near Fairmount Place and two flats; most lots are deep and only partly built. Large areas west of Fairview Avenue are open land with only lot lines. Fairview Avenue is drawn 50 feet wide, Fairview Terrace 37 feet and the cross streets 40 to 50 feet. A heavy dog-legged line separates this part from the turned right part of the sheet, which continues Fairview Avenue south of Fairmount Place.
notes: Fairview Avenue is today North Farview Avenue north of Route 4 and South Farview Avenue south of it.
Prospect is today West Prospect Street (west of Farview) and Prospect Street (east).
Fairview Terrace is today Farview Terrace.
Maple Avenue is today Maple Street.
Richard Avenue, marked not open, has no modern counterpart.
Placed by a helmert from six junctions all on Fairview Avenue (two hand-picked): medium confidence across the avenue, low away from it.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy dog-legged line: part 1 (right, turned about 36 degrees) Fairview Avenue from Fairmount Place south to Pleasant Avenue with Aradale Road, Mildred, Gertrude, Cloverdale, Westview Avenues and Ridgeland Road, Fairview Fire Co. No. 1; part 2 (left, north nearly up) Fairview Avenue from Prospect Street to Fairmount Place with Fairview Terrace, Maple, Spring Valley, Richard and Helen Avenues. Fairmount Place is drawn on both parts.

sheet-5-2.description: The left part of sheet 5 of the 1930 Sanborn atlas of Paramus, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points about 30 degrees to the right of the top of the page. It shows a long stretch of Paramus Road (house numbers 507 to 531) in the southwest of the borough, from Swamp Road, which crosses the Saddle River at the top left at the borough limit, south past Arcadian Avenue and Mackay Avenue. Near the top Paramus Road forks, a branch running north-east off the sheet. The part is sparsely built: the Arcola Manor Hotel, a large two storey frame building, stands on the east side of the road, with the Paramus Episcopal Church (stone, heated by steam, with electric light) further south, a filling station with gasoline tanks at Arcadian Avenue and a few frame dwellings. Arcadian and Mackay Avenues are a small subdivision of narrow lots in blocks 41 and 42, partly built with dwellings; block 40 east of the road and block 60 west of it are largely open. Streets are drawn 45 to 50 feet wide. The heavy line on the right separates this part from the Mount Saint Andrews and Paramus Road parts of the same sheet.
notes: Swamp Road is today Red Mill Road, which follows its line across the Saddle River.

Placed by a helmert from three junctions on Paramus Road (Mackay Avenue detected; Arcadian Avenue and Swamp Road hand-picked): low confidence. The fitted scale (4.33 px per ft) is 11 percent larger than the scale bar, which suggests the 1930 Swamp Road junction lies some 20 m north of today's Red Mill Road junction.

Scale 100 ft. Five parts separated by heavy lines: part 1 (bottom right, largest) Ridgewood Country Club; part 2 (left) Paramus Road from Swamp Road (today Red Mill Road) south past Arcadian and Mackay Avenues, Arcola Manor Hotel, Paramus Episcopal Church, north up-right about 30 degrees; part 3 (top middle) Paramus Road house numbers 601-636 with no cross street; part 4 (top right) Paramus Road at Ridgewood Avenue and Coolidge Boulevard (today Legion Place), Harold Street; part 5 (bottom middle) Mount Saint Andrews Catholic Home on Midland Avenue.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: Ridgewood Country Club (no street drawn; needs step 6b from club buildings or a historic aerial).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Paramus Road, house numbers 601-636 (blocks 27, 28) (a single street with no named cross street, so position along Paramus Road is not fixed; needs a hand-picked feature shared with modern data or a historic aerial).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Mount Saint Andrews Catholic Home on Midland Avenue (only Midland Avenue is drawn, no junction; needs step 6b: anchor on a surviving building or the drive, with Midland Avenue for rotation).

sheet-5-4.description: The top right part of sheet 5 of the 1930 Sanborn atlas of Paramus, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows Paramus Road (house numbers 801 to 837) running up the page in the north of the borough near the Ridgewood line, with Ridgewood Avenue crossing it near the bottom and Coolidge Boulevard leaving it to the east, where Harold runs north from Coolidge Boulevard. The part is thinly built: a few frame dwellings, a coop and outbuildings on the west side of Paramus Road in block 15, and on the east side, in blocks 13, 14 and 17, dwellings, an office and an auto repair garage with gasoline tanks at the corner of Ridgewood Avenue. Much of the west side is marked no exposures. Below Ridgewood Avenue only the corners of blocks 22 and 23 are drawn. Ridgewood Avenue is drawn 45 feet wide and Coolidge Boulevard 60 feet. A large compass rose sits in the open land of block 15. Heavy lines separate this part from the Paramus Road part to its left and from the Mount Saint Andrews and Ridgewood Country Club parts below.
notes: Coolidge Boulevard is today Legion Place, identified from its distance along Paramus Road from Ridgewood Avenue.
Ridgewood Avenue at Paramus Road is today East Ridgewood Avenue.
The drawn Harold does not match the position of today's Harold Street and was not used.
Placed by a helmert from two junctions on Paramus Road: low confidence; the fitted scale (4.13 px per ft) is about 6 percent larger than the scale bar.
